provisions.summary: Raises the standard deduction in steps: amounts for 2024, 2026, 2028, 2030 and 2031. The amounts differ by tax year within 2027-2031, so the spec cannot hold them.
provisions.quote: For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027: (i) $18,000 in the case of a joint return

provisions.summary: Widens the income tax brackets for joint filers and surviving spouses. One schedule applies after Dec 31, 2026 (2027-2028) and another after Dec 31, 2028 (2029-2031).
provisions.quote: In the case of any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028: If the taxable income is: The tax shall be: Not over $38,400 1.40% of taxable income

provisions.summary: Widens the income tax brackets for heads of household. One schedule applies after Dec 31, 2026 and another after Dec 31, 2028.
provisions.quote: Not over $28,800 1.40% of taxable income Over $28,800 but $403.00 plus 3.20% of not over $36,000 excess over $28,800

provisions.summary: Widens the income tax brackets for single filers and married filing separately. One schedule applies after Dec 31, 2026 and another after Dec 31, 2028.
provisions.quote: Not over $19,200 1.40% of taxable income Over $19,200 but $269.00 plus 3.20% of not over $24,000 excess over $19,200

notes: The standard deduction is not modeled. The bill sets different amounts for 2027, 2028, 2030 and 2031, so rule 6 applies; the 2027 level would be the $16,000/$12,000/$8,000 set for years after 2025. The bracket schedules are modeled exactly: the first vintage is the after-December-31-2026 schedule (2027-2028) and the second is the after-December-31-2028 schedule (2029-2031). The bill does not change the capital gains rate, the EITC, the food/excise credit or the personal exemption, so those keys are omitted. The bill is written against pre-Act-24 law (effective for tax years after 2023, amounts from 2024), so it is a backtest sample and not a live proposal. Section 3 (statutory style) and Section 4 (applicability to tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2023) are not provisions.
